MIXED ROTATIONCyclicals +0.0% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The rotation is a one-way bet on real assets and inflation-sensitives, and you should not fight it. Energy leads both the one-month (+6.45%) and year-to-date (+40.33%) sector boards, and the XLE/XLU cyclical versus defensive ratio sits in the top 2% of its yearly range with a z-score of 2.16. Gold miners are the strongest theme by a wide margin at +11.5% one-month, and GDX/GLD is the single most stretched ratio in the entire dataset at a z of 2.46, in the top 1% of its yearly range. Every risk-on signal confirms the same positioning: XLF/XLU is in the top 2% of its yearly range (z 1.87), HYG/LQD is in the top 4% (z 2.21), and SPY/IEF is in the top 0% of its range (z 1.95). The market is telling you that nominal growth expectations are being repriced higher, and cyclical relative to defensive leadership is the cleanest expression of that.

The tension sits underneath: this is a narrowing, not a broadening, market. The AI infra basket is up +100.7% year-to-date, semis up +72.9%, cyber up +61.9%, but the Mag 7 basket is only up +6.1% year-to-date and just +1.0% over the past month. Industrials dropped -5.05% in the last month and consumer discretionary dropped -3.98%. You have energy and miners ripping while the highest-beta growth leadership stalls. The XLRE/SPY ratio is in the bottom 0% of its yearly range (z -2.01), XLY/SPY in the bottom 1% (z -1.89), and XLU/SPY in the bottom 3% (z -1.93). Real assets and commodity-adjacent cyclicals are absorbing all the capital while rate-sensitive defensives and consumer names bleed relative strength. This is an inflation regime, not a broad risk-on stampede.

The stretched-extremes board is flashing caution on the exact positions that have worked. GDX/GLD at a z of 2.46 and XLE/XLU at 2.16 are both deep in the top 2% of their yearly ranges. HYG/IEF at 1.92 (top 2%) and SPY/TLT at 1.96 (top 3%) tell you credit and equities are pricing zero stress against long duration. That is a crowded trade. When every cyclical-versus-defensive ratio is simultaneously in the top few percent of its yearly range, the marginal buyer is exhausted. You keep the energy and miners exposure because the trend momentum is undeniable, but you size new adds smaller. The tell for a reversal is a one-week close in XLE/XLU below its prior month's low, or GDX/GLD printing a weekly close in red after a z-score this extreme.

Real assets and commodity cyclicals are ripping while rate-sensitive defensives and consumer names roll over, making this a narrowing inflation trade rather than a broad risk-on regime.

BULL

Energy up +6.45% in one month and +40.33% year-to-date, gold miners up +11.5% one-month, and XLE/XLU plus XLF/XLU both in the top 2% of their yearly ranges confirm cyclical leadership on multiple timeframes.

BEAR

XLRE/SPY and XLY/SPY sit in the bottom 1% or worse of their yearly ranges, industrials fell -5.05% in the last month, and the Mag 7 is only up +1.0% one-month, signaling deterioration below the surface of the headline leaders.

TELL

Watch XLE/XLU for a weekly close below its prior month's low, or GDX/GLD printing a red weekly candle after a z-score of 2.46, as the signal that the real-asset trade is done.

⚠ Sector breadth leaders are expanding in energy and miners, with XLE/XLU and XLF/XLU both in the top **2%** of yearly ranges, suggesting a broadening cyclical advance. vs The Mag 7 basket is up only **+1.0%** one-month and **+6.1%** year-to-date, while industrials and discretionary dropped **-5.05%** and **-3.98%** over the same month, indicating a narrowing market concentrated in commodity and real-asset cyclicals only.: Trust the theme and sector extremes over the Mag 7: the z-scores on cyclical-versus-defensive ratios are extreme in one direction while the mega-cap growth complex stagnates, meaning the 'broadening' is a rotation out of growth into real assets, not a broad market lift.
⚠ HYG/LQD is in the top **4%** of its yearly range and HYG/IEF in the top **2%**, signaling credit investors see zero default risk and are fully in risk-on mode. vs XLRE/SPY is in the bottom **0%** and VIXY/SPY in the bottom **1%**, indicating real estate and volatility hedges are being abandoned at historically extreme rates, which typically marks late-cycle complacency rather than early-cycle confidence.: Trust the complacency read from the haven and real estate extremes over the credit strength: when volatility and rate-sensitive real estate are at yearly lows simultaneously with credit at yearly highs, the marginal investor has already accumulated all the risk, and the asymmetry favors a snap-back in the neglected defensive assets.

GDX/GLD at a z of 2.46 (top 1% of yearly range), XLE/XLU at 2.16 (top 2%), and IBB/XLV at 2.13 (top 1%) are mean-reversion candidates despite strong trend support, because all three are crowded cyclical linkages that have run to statistical extremes in a single direction. HYG/IEF at a z of 1.92 (top 2%) and SPY/IEF at 1.95 (top 0%) tell you credit and equity risk premiums are priced for perfection against the front end, and those compressions tend to unwind violently when they crack. The exceptions that confirm trend rather than reversion are XLE/XLU and SPY/TLT at z 1.96, because the underlying fundamentals of energy earnings and equity dominance over bonds align with the multi-month trend, and these ratios have staying power until the fundamental regime shifts.
